THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Weeknight Picanha with Chimichurri & Frozen Greens

One skillet for the picanha, a second skillet for the frozen greens, and the same steak skillet reheats the kid chicken patties + toasts the slider buns. 480 cal / 40g protein per adult plate. Costco chimichurri is the shortcut — homemade No-Judge Chimichurri is the alternative if you want full control.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME25 min
COOK METHODCast iron
EST. / SERVING~480 cal | ~40g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: TWO SKILLETS, TWO HEATS. Steak skillet HOT (medium-high, avocado spray). Vegetable skillet MEDIUM (per the package). Do not try to share.

Ingredients

SHARED VEGETABLE

  • 3 label servings Whole Foods Market European Greens with Basil & Garlic Sauce (1 per adult + 1/2 per kid)

ADULT PROTEIN

  • 12 oz picanha steaks total (6 oz per adult)

Option 1

  • 4 fully-cooked chicken breakfast patties (Amylu — 2 per kid)
  • 2 slider buns (1 per kid, split + toasted)

PAN OIL

  • Avocado-oil cooking spray

ADULT SAUCE

  • 2 label servings prepared chimichurri (1 per adult — Fotis Fine Foods from Costco or the No-Judge Chimichurri cookbook version)

Allergens: gluten. Kid bun gluten

AT THE PROTEIN + CARB — different meat + different carb per plate. Same frozen greens on both plates (full serving adult / half serving kid). Adult sauce (chimichurri) is skipped on the kid plate.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.SALT THE PICANHA. Season both sides of 12 oz picanha with salt. No other seasoning — the chimichurri carries the flavor.
  2. 2.START THE GREENS. Add 3 label servings frozen European greens to a medium skillet. Cook per the package — usually 6-8 min at medium heat, stirring occasionally.
  3. 3.SEAR THE PICANHA. Heat a second skillet on medium-high, coat lightly with avocado spray, add the picanha. Press briefly for full pan contact if needed. Sear + flip until browned and cooked to preferred doneness.
  4. 4.DONENESS + SAFETY. Creator pulls at 135°F for medium (video honestly notes this cook landed closer to medium-well). USDA recommends whole beef steaks cook to 145°F + rest 3 min before slicing. Both are valid — present them as separate choices.
  5. 5.REST + SLICE. Transfer picanha to a board and rest 5+ min. Then slice thin against the grain.

Adult — 6 oz Picanha + Basil-Garlic Frozen Greens + Costco Chimichurri

  1. 6.PLATE THE ADULT. 6 oz sliced picanha + 1 serving basil-garlic frozen greens.
  2. 7.SPOON THE CHIMICHURRI. 1 serving of prepared chimichurri over the sliced steak. Stir the jar thoroughly first — the oil separates during storage.

Kid — Chicken Patties + Half-Serving Greens + Toasted Slider Bun (Deconstructed) · Option 1

  1. 6.REHEAT KID PATTIES. Once the picanha comes out to rest, drop 4 chicken breakfast patties into the same steak skillet on medium heat. Reheat 2-3 min per side per package directions.
  2. 7.TOAST SLIDER BUNS. Split 2 slider buns. Cut heat to medium-low so the beef fat doesn't burn. Bun halves cut-side-down for 60 sec until golden.
  3. 8.PLATE KID. Chop patties into age-appropriate pieces. Divided tray: 2 chopped patties in one compartment, 1/2 serving greens in another, 1 toasted slider bun in a third. No forced sandwich build — kid decides.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — 6 oz Picanha + Basil-Garlic Frozen Greens + Costco Chimichurri: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — Chicken Patties + Half-Serving Greens + Toasted Slider Bun (Deconstructed): Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • SALT ONLY ON THE PICANHA. No pepper, no rub, no garlic powder. The chimichurri carries every other flavor note; a rub muddies the hand-off. Salt both sides before the steak hits the pan.
  • REST THE STEAK 5+ MIN BEFORE SLICING. Rested steak keeps its juices; hot-sliced steak bleeds them onto the board. Use the rest window to reheat kid patties + toast buns in the steak skillet.

If something fails

Picanha overcooks past medium-rare / medium: Skillet was too hot for the fat cap, or the steak stayed on too long after the flip. Pull the picanha 5-10°F below the target — carryover cooking will finish it during the rest. Creator pulls at 135°F for medium; USDA recommends 145°F + 3 min rest. If you overshoot, slice thin against the grain and lean on the chimichurri.

Frozen greens are watery on the plate: Skillet wasn't hot enough at the end, or the pan was crowded. Cook per the package but finish the last 60-90 sec at higher heat to boil off surface moisture. If the sauce still looks thin, drain the greens briefly in a mesh strainer before plating.

Costco chimichurri is too vinegary / too oily: Jars vary. Stir the jar thoroughly before spooning — oil separates during storage. If it's still off-balance, cut it 1:1 with fresh parsley + a squeeze of lemon, or switch to the No-Judge Chimichurri cookbook recipe for full control.

Kids reject the chicken patties whole: Chop into age-appropriate pieces before plating — the video shows Amylu patties chopped into thirds. Deconstructed tray, patty pieces in one compartment, greens in another, toasted bun in a third. No forced sandwich build.

Slider buns burn in the steak skillet: Fat left over from the picanha is HOT — cut heat to medium-low before adding the buns, cut-side-down for 60 seconds only. Watch the color; pull as soon as they're golden.

Adult plate feels flat / one-note: Not enough chimichurri, or the jar hadn't been stirred before spooning. Add a second half-serving — the acid + herb bite is what carries the steak into 'restaurant-plate' territory. Or squeeze a lemon wedge for a tighter finish.

Storage and reheating

Store: Cool cooked picanha, chicken patties, and greens promptly and refrigerate in separate airtight containers within 2 hours. Chimichurri stays sealed per jar directions. Slider buns keep sealed at room temp; do not pre-assemble.

Reheat: Steak: gentle reheat — cast-iron on medium-low or 300°F oven for 5-6 min to keep the interior from pushing past medium. Chicken patties: same skillet reheat, 2-3 min per side. Greens: covered pan on medium 2-3 min. Bring all leftovers to 165°F. Assemble the toasted-bun kid plate fresh.

Lasts: Cooked leftovers 3-4 days fridge (per USDA leftovers guidance). Refrigerated Costco chimichurri per its jar. Slider buns: sealed at room temp per label, or freeze for longer hold.

Make this when

You want steak-night flavor on a weeknight without making every component from scratch. Two shortcuts do the heavy lifting: Whole Foods Market frozen European greens with a basil-and-garlic sauce (no chop, no wash) and Fotis Fine Foods refrigerated chimichurri from Costco (no herb-mince, no rest time). The kid plate is a familiar chicken-patty + slider-bun tray so the same 25-minute cook feeds everyone.

Brands I use

Whole Foods Market
European Greens with Basil & Garlic Sauce (frozen)
The freezer-to-plate vegetable shortcut. Basil-and-garlic sauce built into the bag — no chop, no wash, no separate sauce. 3 label servings feeds 2 adults full + 2 kids half. Sub Kirkland European Vegetable Blend or any similar frozen blend.
Fotis Fine Foods
Chimichurri (24 oz, refrigerated) — Costco
The adult sauce shortcut. Current Costco listing calls out a 1 tbsp (15g) serving. Stir the jar thoroughly before spooning — oil separates during storage. Verify the jar in hand; formulas can change. Homemade alternative: the No-Judge Chimichurri cookbook entry.
Amylu
Chicken Breakfast Patties (fully cooked)
The kid protein anchor. Fully cooked, pork-free, reheats in the steak skillet in 2-3 min per side. Chopped into age-appropriate pieces for the deconstructed tray. Sub any fully-cooked chicken patty or a chopped rotisserie portion. Verify the exact patty flavor before publishing label claims.
No-Judge Chimichurri
Cookbook cross-link — the homemade alternative
This dinner uses a refrigerated Costco chimichurri on purpose (weeknight shortcut). If you want full control over herbs, garlic, and acid, the No-Judge Chimichurri cookbook entry is the swap. Prefer homemade? Use the No-Judge Chimichurri instead.
